response:
DISCOVERY: none.

Scoped null-find justification: I reviewed `add_round_findings`, cache invalidation, equivalence-class construction, `_novel_classes`, suppression weighting, `kappa_set`, `kappa_rate`, `kappa_adopt`, `converged`, `estimate_gamma`, and the static validators. The substantive CRITICAL/HIGH candidates I found collapse to existing registry entries: novel-class masking maps to C0014, unregistered-round convergence maps to C0010/C0018, cross-flaw clustering maps to C0019/C0020, decreasing cumulative class count maps to C0012/C0005, invalid durations map to C0015. I found no distinct new CRITICAL/HIGH issue and no quick MEDIUM issue worth filing separately.

CONFIRM C0014 | Evidence: `_novel_classes()` classifies an entire current-round equivalence class as non-novel if any member matches a prior finding. Concrete trace: prior round has `P` with severity `0.1`; current round has `D` similar to `P`, and `H` similar to `D` but not to `P`, with severity `0.95`. `_compute_equivalence_classes([D, H])` places `D` and `H` in one current class. `_novel_classes()` sees `D ~ P`, sets `is_novel=False`, and drops the whole class, so `H` is not counted as novel and `_veto()` does not fire. That is a confirmed HIGH correctness failure in novelty/veto detection.

CONFIRM C0018 | Evidence: public methods do not reject unregistered `round_idx`. Concrete trace after registering rounds `0` and `1`, call `converged(99)`. `kappa_set(99)` uses empty current findings and cumulative findings from known prior rounds, so novelty is zero and set stability tends high. `kappa_rate(99)` uses empty round-99 classes, so current rate is zero and rate stability tends high if baseline is nonzero. `kappa_adopt(99)` defaults missing adoption delta to `0.0`, returning `1.0`. If `99 >= min_rounds_for_convergence` and no veto exists, `converged(99)` can return true for a round that never executed. This confirms the interface/correctness bug.

CONFIRM C0015 | Evidence: `add_round_findings()` accepts `duration <= 0`, and `_rate()` later computes `len(classes) / max(dt, 1e-10)`. Concrete trace: `add_round_findings(1, [finding], duration=-5.0)` stores `-5.0`; `kappa_rate(1)` evaluates the rate denominator as `1e-10`, producing an artificial rate of `10_000_000_000` for one finding. This silently converts invalid input into extreme convergence/divergence signal instead of rejecting it at the interface boundary.

CONFIRM C0019 | Evidence: `_compute_equivalence_classes()` unions findings solely on `similarity_fn(...) >= tau_sim`; it does not require matching `flaw_class`. Concrete trace: a security flaw and a documentation flaw with similar text above `tau_sim` are merged into one `FindingEquivalenceClass`; the resulting `flaw_class` is then assigned from `members[0].flaw_class`, making the class category order-dependent. This can corrupt per-class novelty, severity veto interpretation, and registry statistics. Confirmed.

MERGE C0019 <- C0020 | Evidence: C0019 and C0020 have the same root cause: equivalence-class clustering ignores `flaw_class` and relies only on textual similarity. C0020 should merge into C0019 as the canonical issue unless the registry prefers the lower-numbered canonical already assigned by the runner.

CONFIRM C0012 | Evidence: `estimate_gamma()` returns `0.0` when `cum_r < cum_1`. Concrete trace: round 1 cumulative classes are `{A, B}` with count `2`; round 2 introduces a bridging finding `C` similar enough under single-linkage to merge `A` and `B`, so cumulative classes become `{A,B,C}` with count `1`. The code path is `if cum_r <= cum_1: return 1.0 if cum_r == cum_1 else 0.0`, so it returns `0.0`. That is not a neutral “no convergence” case; it is an artefact of cross-round clustering reducing class count, and returning `0.0` silently misreports the diagnostic.

CHALLENGE C0004 | Evidence: under the apparent intended invariants `severity >= 0` and `0 <= suppression_weight <= 1`, `kappa_set()` is not unbounded below despite lacking an explicit clamp. Derivation: for every novel class `ec`, `_weighted_novel_severity` contributes `w(ec) * ec.aggregated_severity`, with `w(ec) <= 1`, so contribution is `<= ec.aggregated_severity`. Each novel current class is included in the cumulative class set for the same round; non-novel and prior classes add nonnegative severity to the denominator. Therefore `novel_sev <= total_sev_without_epsilon`, so `novel_sev / (total_sev + epsilon) < 1`, hence `kappa_set() > 0`. Also `novel_sev >= 0`, so `kappa_set() <= 1`. Falsifier: if `Finding.severity` can be negative or `config.w_floor > 1`, the proof fails, but that would be a missing input-validation issue, not the stated overflow mechanism. Under valid config/data invariants, C0004 should be rejected or narrowed.
